Where it began

Nahid Rana was born on 2 October 2002 and grew up in Chapai Nawabganj district, where his cricket was played with a tennis ball wrapped in tape. He did not bowl with a proper hard ball until 2020, when he had finished his Higher Secondary School Certificate and began training at an academy in Rajshahi.

At first he was a net bowler, sending the ball down to the Rajshahi Division batters. He sent it down so fast that the scouts soon noticed, and in October 2021 he made his first-class debut for Rajshahi Division in the National Cricket League.

The player

He rose quickly. He finished the 2022–23 season of the National Cricket League with 32 wickets, second only to one other bowler, including his first five-wicket haul, against Barishal Division. On his Twenty20 debut for Khulna Tigers in January 2023 he bowled at around 140 to 150 km/h throughout, and people across the country began to talk about him.

His Test debut came in May 2024, at home to Sri Lanka in Sylhet. A few months later, in the second Test in Pakistan, his bowling in the third innings helped Bangladesh to a historic 2–0 series win. By November 2026 he had played 12 Tests and taken 38 wickets, with a best of 5 for 40 and two five-wicket hauls.

What made him special

Pace, plain and simple. A bowler who can keep the speed up through a long spell is a rare thing, and Bangladesh were glad to have one. In July 2026 he took 6 for 21 against Zimbabwe, the best one-day figures by a Bangladesh bowler up to then.

Batting was not really his department. His 21 Test runs had come at 2.62 by November 2026, though with 11 not-outs from 19 innings he had shown he could hang around while someone else did the scoring.

Away from the middle

He was part of the Bangladesh squad that took bronze at the 2022 Asian Games, held in late 2023, even if he did not get a match. He was picked for the 2025 Champions Trophy, and his franchise career took off too. In January 2026 he took 3 for 11 for Rangpur Riders against Dhaka Capitals, and that year he joined Peshawar Zalmi in the Pakistan Super League. He took nine wickets in five games as they won the title for the first time in nine years.

And finally

He started out bowling to Rajshahi batters in the nets, purely to help them practise. Somewhere there may be a few batters who can say they faced him first, and who are very glad he moved on.
